newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Decision close on NZ's Peters contempt allegation.
newsitem.headline: Decision close on NZ's Peters contempt allegation.

text.p: The New Zealand Parliament's powerful privileges committee was due to meet behind closed doors late on Wednesday to complete its consideration of an allegation of contempt of parliament against Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer Winston Peters.
After a two hour meeting on Tuesday, committee chairman and Attorney General Paul East said the panel was making good progress and hoped to reach a decision later in the day.
The eight-member committee is equally divided between the government and opposition parties. Parliamentary sources said the matter could yet go to the full parliament for debate.
"The government (MPs) are solidly behind Peters," one opposition MP said.
The committee will not release its findings until the House sits again on April 22, East said.
The contempt allegation against Peters was made by left-wing Alliance leader Jim Anderton after a fracas between Peters and government backbencher John Banks on March 5.

Banks and Anderton said in evidence Peters had assaulted and threatened Banks outside the debating chamber after a close division over legislation to delay tax cuts. Peters said he only put a hand on Banks to indicate he wanted to continue talking.
The privileges committee is also due to consider a complaint, lodged by Anderton as a petition to the committee, about a second incident on March 5.

Anderton said Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare allegedly manhandled a radio journalist who was trying to record the exchange between Banks and Peters. Henare has apologised to the journalist for the incident.
Peters and Henare are leader and deputy leader respectively of nationalist New Zealand First, the junior partner in New Zealand's coalition government.
